intent: Phase 1 of NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md's 250-line-cap campaign: bring focus_owner/android/.../DevicePolicyBridge.kt (415 lines) under the cap.
changes: Kotlin has no part-of mechanism like Dart, so the class was split by extracting three cohesive method groups into standalone internal helper classes, each held as a private delegate field on DevicePolicyBridge: DevicePolicyVpnDns (always-on-VPN + Private DNS pinning), DevicePolicyLocation (self-grant location permissions + enable location), DevicePolicyUninstallGuard (self/package uninstall blocking)

DevicePolicyBridge's public API is unchanged -- every public method (setAlwaysOnVpn, setVpnConfigBlocked, grantLocationPermissions, setSelfUninstallBlocked, etc.) still exists on DevicePolicyBridge as a one-line delegating wrapper, since MainActivity.kt and EnforcementService.kt call these directly on a DevicePolicyBridge instance and were not touched
No behavioral change: all moved method bodies are verbatim, including doc comments explaining the DPM quirks and measured device behavior each guards against
DevicePolicyBridge.kt: 415 -> 219 lines; three new files at 146/92/79 lines

verification.evidence: DevicePolicyBridge.kt off the list; file count over cap dropped from 10 to 9
BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no compile errors -- confirms the delegate wiring (constructor params, function-reference callbacks for isDeviceOwner/isProfileOwner) type-checks correctly

BUILD SUCCESSFUL; test-results XML shows 40 tests total (6+9+12+13 across 4 suites), 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. --rerun-tasks used per NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md's Kotlin verification note (a plain gradlew test can report UP-TO-DATE and prove nothing)

risks: No dedicated unit test exists for DevicePolicyBridge itself (it wraps the real Android DevicePolicyManager system service, not unit-testable without instrumentation), so this split relies on compile-time type-checking plus the unchanged public API surface as its correctness argument, not a passing test asserting DevicePolicyBridge's own behavior

The isDeviceOwner/isProfileOwner function-reference pattern used to wire delegates (::isDeviceOwner passed into constructors) means each helper calls back into DevicePolicyBridge on every check rather than caching a value -- matches the original code's behavior (which also called isDeviceOwner() fresh each time) but is a slightly less obvious pattern than a plain boolean field
rollback: After rollback, re-run gradlew compileDebugKotlin --rerun-tasks to confirm the pre-split file still compiles clean
